messages:
Alex: Heads-up — planning to flip feature flag `new-scheduler-v2` for a 5% canary tomorrow at 2026-04-02 10:00 UTC. Quick roll call: who can own smoke checks, who handles rollback?

Jen: I can own smoke checks. Will verify job success rates + latency dashboards. Which endpoints should I focus on?

Alex: Primary surface is the scheduling API (`POST /v1/schedule`) and background worker job runner. Plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with ~30m observation windows. Default stays OFF; canary via `user_segment=canary`. Toggle commands:
```
# enable 5% canary
feature-flag set new-scheduler-v2 true --percent=5 --env=prod
# increase to 25%
feature-flag set new-scheduler-v2 true --percent=25 --env=prod
```

Chris: I'll own rollback and watch logs. Rollback quick command:
```
feature-flag set new-scheduler-v2 false --env=prod && kubectl rollout restart deployment/scheduler -n prod
```
Keep me in the loop and paste any failing traces.

Maya: Note: dedicated GPU pool is at ~85% right now; if the canary causes more parallel scheduling we may need to bump autoscale or throttle concurrency. I'll be available to adjust autoscaling for the window. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Maintenance window reserved: 2026-04-02 10:00 UTC — canary rollout for `new-scheduler-v2`. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/scheduler-canary (read-only).

Jen: Smoke checklist I'll run and post results here: 1) create sample job end-to-end 2) verify job completion time within baseline ±10% 3) check error count for /v1/schedule 4) confirm P95 latency <150ms 5) tail worker errors for 30m.

Alex: Great — I'll push the 5% toggle at 10:00 and ping this thread. If anything looks off, use Chris' rollback command. Tagging @Chris @Jen @Maya for visibility.

Chris: Ack. I'll be on call 10:00–11:30 UTC and monitoring `/logs/scheduler-canary`. If I need to escalate, I'll ping @sam-sre and post snippets here. :thumbsup:
